ops.description: The watchdisc lane's codex adversarial review surfaced parse-layer parity divergences affecting ALL consumers (watch delegates to parse_entry; triaged out-of-scope there). Fix in a dedicated lane AFTER the queryfacts lane lands (both touch rust/crates/core/src/parse.rs — conflict risk while in flight). Items: (1) empty `usage:{}` drop semantics; (2) value type-filtering at parse (cwd:7, isSidechain:1 must preserve per trap #4); (3) tool-result non-str/list content handling; (4) empty toolDenialKind fallback; (5) huge-int/inf materialization behavior; (6) naive/leap-second timestamp parsing vs Python fromisoformat; (7) whitespace-driven interrupted/agent-injected flags (protocol.rs/filterspec boundary — check against Python str semantics per trap #1); (8) NESTED-object field reads during struct construction (usage fields, message internals) read first-wins pre-normalization; (9) ROOT identity-key dups (uuid/sessionId/timestamp) read first-wins — deliberately deferred with MEASURED constraint: any full root-key dedup costs 274ns/record ≈ 7-13% of the 2.08µs/record parse (smallmods micro + criterion, cross-validated), far over the ≤2% hot-path budget; only the `type` dispatch read is last-wins (~1.1%). Items 8-9 are likely PERMANENT accepted divergences unless a zero-cost trick appears (dup detection inside sonic's parse isn't accessible without patching sonic) — the Python reference dies at P6, making Rust behavior the contract for these never-occurring inputs. Each remaining item: reproduce vs Python first, mirror exactly, pin in parse-level golden/unit tests, and respect the ≤2% parse budget. Read traps doc 62cd44cd first. MUST land before P3 gates.
